%% Version A: Monotonic scaling narrative (7B < 14B < 32B degeneracy)
%% Use condition: Qwen2.5 FT results show degeneracy rising monotonically with scale.
%% Status: Placeholder framework — fill numbers when exp results arrive.

%% ---- Placeholder commands (replace with actual values) ----
\newcommand{\scaleSevenDegen}{XX.X}    % 7B degeneracy %
\newcommand{\scaleFourteenDegen}{XX.X} % 14B degeneracy %
\newcommand{\scaleThirtytwoDegen}{XX.X}% 32B degeneracy %
\newcommand{\scaleSevenGreedy}{.XXX}   % 7B greedy F1
\newcommand{\scaleFourteenGreedy}{.XXX}% 14B greedy F1
\newcommand{\scaleThirtytwoGreedy}{.XXX}% 32B greedy F1
\newcommand{\scaleSevenConstr}{X.XX}   % 7B construction Δ (pp)
\newcommand{\scaleFourteenConstr}{X.XX}% 14B construction Δ (pp)
\newcommand{\scaleThirtytwoConstr}{X.XX}% 32B construction Δ (pp)
\newcommand{\scaleSevenLP}{.XXX}       % 7B LP ρ
\newcommand{\scaleFourteenLP}{.XXX}    % 14B LP ρ
\newcommand{\scaleThirtytwoLP}{.XXX}   % 32B LP ρ

%% ---- Narrative ----

\paragraph{Degeneracy rises with scale within a model family.}
To examine how model scale affects the capability--diversity tradeoff, we fine-tune Qwen2.5 at three scales (7B, 14B, 32B) with an identical QLoRA recipe on Few-NERD ($N{=}8$, $T{=}1.0$).
Degeneracy increases monotonically with parameter count: $\scaleSevenDegen\%\to\scaleFourteenDegen\%\to\scaleThirtytwoDegen\%$ (Figure~\ref{fig:scaling_curve}a).
Greedy F1 also rises ($\scaleSevenGreedy\to\scaleFourteenGreedy\to\scaleThirtytwoGreedy$), confirming that larger models are more capable but less diverse in their sampled outputs.
LP-weighted construction $\Delta$F1 inversely tracks degeneracy ($\scaleSevenConstr\to\scaleFourteenConstr\to\scaleThirtytwoConstr$\,pp), consistent with the gating hypothesis from \S\ref{sec:fewnerd}: the selection window narrows as stronger greedy performance comes at the cost of reduced output diversity.

This within-family trend converges with two independent dimensions of evidence.
Along the \emph{epoch} dimension, extending Qwen3-8B training from 3 to 5 epochs on Few-NERD raises degeneracy from 11.1\% to 31.3\% (\S\ref{sec:fewnerd}), mirroring the effect of added parameters.
Along the \emph{family} dimension, Qwen3-8B FT (13.0\% degeneracy, $+1.39$\,pp construction) and Qwen2.5-72B ZS (46.2\%, $-0.20$\,pp) bracket the trade-off from opposite ends.
Across all three dimensions---scale, training duration, and model family---higher degeneracy consistently predicts smaller or negative construction gains, supporting degeneracy as a robust diagnostic for when self-consistency aggregation can add value.

%% Version B: Non-monotonic scaling narrative (some scale point breaks monotonicity)
%% Use condition: Qwen2.5 FT results show degeneracy does NOT rise monotonically with scale.
%% Status: Placeholder framework — fill numbers when exp results arrive.

%% ---- Placeholder commands (replace with actual values) ----
\newcommand{\scaleSevenDegen}{XX.X}    % 7B degeneracy %
\newcommand{\scaleFourteenDegen}{XX.X} % 14B degeneracy %
\newcommand{\scaleThirtytwoDegen}{XX.X}% 32B degeneracy %
\newcommand{\scaleSevenGreedy}{.XXX}   % 7B greedy F1
\newcommand{\scaleFourteenGreedy}{.XXX}% 14B greedy F1
\newcommand{\scaleThirtytwoGreedy}{.XXX}% 32B greedy F1
\newcommand{\scaleSevenConstr}{X.XX}   % 7B construction Δ (pp)
\newcommand{\scaleFourteenConstr}{X.XX}% 14B construction Δ (pp)
\newcommand{\scaleThirtytwoConstr}{X.XX}% 32B construction Δ (pp)
\newcommand{\scaleSevenLP}{.XXX}       % 7B LP ρ
\newcommand{\scaleFourteenLP}{.XXX}    % 14B LP ρ
\newcommand{\scaleThirtytwoLP}{.XXX}   % 32B LP ρ

%% ---- Narrative ----

\paragraph{Degeneracy is not a simple function of scale.}
We fine-tune Qwen2.5 at three scales (7B, 14B, 32B) with an identical QLoRA recipe on Few-NERD ($N{=}8$, $T{=}1.0$).
Degeneracy does not increase monotonically with parameter count: $\scaleSevenDegen\%\to\scaleFourteenDegen\%\to\scaleThirtytwoDegen\%$ (Figure~\ref{fig:scaling_curve}a), indicating that model-specific factors beyond raw scale---such as pretraining data composition or architecture choices within the Qwen2.5 family---modulate the capability--diversity tradeoff.
Nonetheless, the gating relationship between degeneracy and construction effectiveness remains intact: LP-weighted construction $\Delta$F1 tracks degeneracy rather than parameter count ($\scaleSevenConstr$, $\scaleFourteenConstr$, $\scaleThirtytwoConstr$\,pp), with the largest gains at the scale point exhibiting lowest degeneracy regardless of model size.

This result reframes degeneracy as a \emph{diagnostic} rather than a predictable consequence of scaling.
The epoch dimension reinforces this view: extending Qwen3-8B training from 3 to 5 epochs on Few-NERD raises degeneracy from 11.1\% to 31.3\% (\S\ref{sec:fewnerd}), showing that training choices can shift degeneracy as much as a $4{\times}$ increase in parameters.
The practical implication is that practitioners should measure degeneracy post-hoc rather than predict it from model size: a mid-scale model with favorable output diversity may benefit more from self-consistency aggregation than a larger model whose samples have collapsed.

两版已写入 artifacts/：

- **Version A**（单调）：degeneracy 随 scale 单调上升 → "selection window narrows" 叙事，与 epoch/family 两维证据汇合，三维一致性支撑 degeneracy 作为 robust diagnostic。
- **Version B**（非单调）：degeneracy 不随 scale 单调变化 → 重新定位 degeneracy 为 post-hoc diagnostic 而非 scaling 的可预测结果，弱化 "narrows with scale" 说法，转向 "practitioners should measure rather than predict"。

两版共享同一套 `\newcommand` placeholder，数据到位后替换即可。每版约 5-6 句，匹配现有 `zeroshot_scaling_draft.tex` 的 `\paragraph{}` 风格和数据密度。
